precepts.text: I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel. No begging for them either.
precepts.point: And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: and I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me. Even after; even after the deliverance, there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us that need to be purged, people that still need to get right, and Christ is the one who is going to give it to them. They shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.

note.label: Forged by Fire

precepts.why:
The Lord pleads with the nations the same way he pleads with Israel. Joel says: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. No baby, baby, please for them either. He will kill them, for his people Israel.

The nations are judged “for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” The pleading in the valley of Jehoshaphat is the Lord's vengeance on the ones who scattered us.

So when Ezekiel says the Lord will plead with Israel face to face in the wilderness “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”, the word means the same thing it means for the nations: judgment, smiting and fire, not begging. He pleads for Israel against the nations, and he pleads with the rebels in Israel in the wilderness, and nobody should read either as the Lord asking nicely.

precepts.text: The days come that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it. We went over this last week. Now we know what Joel 3:1 is saying.
precepts.point: In those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem: meaning he is going to bring us back to our homeland. Here is the evidence.

note.label: America: The New Roman Empire

precepts.why:
Joel opens with “in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Jeremiah shows what that means: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, saith the Lord: and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.”

To bring again the captivity is to bring us back to our homeland, the land given to our fathers, and to possess it. That is the evidence. Now we know what Joel 3:1 is saying.

And it ties the whole chapter together. The Most High gathers all nations into the valley of Jehoshaphat, in Israel, at the place called Har-Megiddo, where the name Armageddon comes from, to plead with them for his people and his heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations while they parted his land between the Arabs and the Edomites.

Joel ends the same way it begins: “Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them”. The Most High raises up the Israelites out of the places they were sold into, back to verse 1, and brings us home to our land in freedom.

precepts.text: For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant. The same people delivered us to Edom, whom Joel calls the Grecians. I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof: the wall of Tyrus is the land, and you see that land catching hell today, and the Arabs are there too.
precepts.point: Here is the part to highlight: the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border. Tyre, Zidon and the Palestinians, the Arabs, sold us to the Grecians, the white man.

note.label: America: The New Roman Empire

precepts.why:
Joel asks, “what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine?” and charges them: “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians”. Amos says the same of Tyre: “For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant”.

The same people delivered us to Edom, whom Joel calls the Grecians: the white man. Tyre and Zidon were the Hamite nations of Canaan back then, and the coasts of Palestine, the ancient Philistines, is the modern name for the modern people there, the Arabs. They cast lots for our people, bid on us the way it is still done in the Arab countries, gave a boy for an harlot, making the men into breeders, and sold a girl for wine. They took our silver and gold and robbed our temples.

“But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof.” The wall of Tyrus is the land, and you see that land catching hell today, and the Arabs are there too.

That is the recompence Joel speaks of: what you did to my people, I will have done to you. They recompensed the Most High by selling us as slaves, so he will sell their sons and daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off. Eye for eye, tooth for tooth. “For the Lord hath spoken it”, and Christians cannot change this Bible.

precepts.text: When I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem: the same words, and Jeremiah explains them as a return from captivity.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.” That book is called the Bible today. Then pay attention: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel 3:1 confuses some brothers: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Read that alone and you think it means he is bringing us back into slavery. That is not what it means.

Go back to Jeremiah 30:3. Notice the same words, except Jeremiah explains them: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” When he says he will bring again the captivity, he is speaking of bringing us back from captivity, not into captivity. Jeremiah explains Joel.

precepts.text: In those days and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem. The same phrase as Jeremiah 30, the return to the land.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. That is the great tribulation.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book”: the Bible. “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel uses the same words: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Sometimes in your thoughts you might be saying that means the Lord is going to make us slaves again. No, that is not what it means.

Jeremiah explains it in the same verse: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” To bring again the captivity is to bring us again to our land. That is the evidence. The same phrase in Joel 3:1 speaks of that same return of Judah and Jerusalem, in those days and in that time, the days of Jacob's trouble, out of which he shall be saved.

precepts.text: When I bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will gather all nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, in the Middle East, and plead with them there for my people and my heritage Israel. The nations' attention is on the Middle East, and right now on America and Iran.
precepts.point: Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, from the rising of the sun, from the south, the Arab nations, from the east, China and India, and Libanus, to turn themselves one against another and repay the things they have done to them.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Ezra's vision says, “Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, which are from the rising of the sun, from the south, from the east, and Libanus; to turn themselves one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them.” From the south, the Arab nations; from the east, China and India. Joel is the precept to it.

“For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. I will gather all nations: that is the calling together of all the kings of the earth in 2 Esdras 15.

The valley of Jehoshaphat is in the Middle East. So what do we see right now? More and more nations are putting their attention on the Middle East, and right now the focus is America and Iran. There the Lord is going to plead with the nations for his people, his heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations.

This is what the prophecies say; the vision is for an appointed time, and at the end it shall speak and not lie. So when we see this war, we are supposed to rejoice and increase our faith. We are drawing closer to Christ's return, so we have to draw closer to each other, fellowship more, fast and pray more.

precepts.text: Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; prepare war, wake up the mighty men; multitudes in the valley of decision.
precepts.point: Put yourselves in array against Babylon; spare no arrows, for she hath sinned against the Lord. As she hath done, do unto her.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
Jeremiah's word is “against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans”. Babylon here is America; the Chaldeans are Amalek, so-called Israel. And it is not just Esau: it is judgment on all the nations. “Put yourselves in array against Babylon round about: all ye that bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she hath sinned against the Lord.” “for it is the vengeance of the Lord: take vengeance upon her; as she hath done, do unto her.”

Joel shows who is called up to do it: “Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up”. The Gentiles are the other nations, and the Lord wants them to prepare war. China, America, Russia, Syria, France, Great Britain, Iran, Saudi Arabia: they all have to go to war. All you military men, wake up. It is time to go to Armageddon.

“Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.” Make weapons; you finished boot camp, now go to war. “Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.” Wake up, Esau; wake up, Ishmael. The valley of Jehoshaphat is the valley of decision, and they have to go there and die.

“Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe”; “for their wickedness is great. Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.” The nations arrayed against Babylon are the sword of the Lord bringing his vengeance on her.

precepts.text: The Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabians.
precepts.point: Tyre, Sidon and the coasts of Palestine, the Hamites, together with the Arabs, sold Israel to the Grecians. Records call slavery the result of raids by Arabs and Hamites on Negro communities.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Joel says the nations “have scattered among the nations, and parted my land”, “cast lots for my people”, and he names who: “O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine”. The Zidonians are Canaanites, Hamites, and the coasts of Palestine are the Arabs. “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” This is nothing new. They did it before, in the days of an evil king named Jehoram.

Jehoram “walked in the way of the kings of Israel”, and in his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and made themselves a king, “because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.” Because of Jehoram’s disobedience and wickedness, God raised up enemies against him.

“Moreover the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians”. The Philistines: that is Tyre and Zidon, the Hamites. And the Arabians, near the other Hamites. “And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.”

So the Hamites and the Arabs got together and stole his wives and his kids. It is their common nature to do that: they steal people. That is the same pair Joel names, and the records say it plainly: slavery in Africa was due to raids of Arabs and Hamites on Negro communities. The Hamite, the Arab and the white man worked together removing us far from our border, and the land is parted today between the Israelis and the Arabs. That is why God will plead with the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat for his people.

precepts.text: Egypt shall be a desolation and Edom a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.”

The law says “thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land.” Many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land. Joel puts Egypt and Edom side by side: both made a desolation, both for the same violence against the children of Judah.

precepts.text: The Most High will plead for his heritage Israel whom the nations scattered and parted his land, casting lots for his people and selling them, and he will return their recompense on their own heads.
precepts.point: They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
The same Most High who gave Judah into the hand of the Chaldees will plead for them. “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.”

The nations “have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine.” They took his silver and his gold and “carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things”, just as all the vessels and treasures of the house of the Lord were carried to Babylon. And “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.”

So the carrying away is not the end of the matter. The nations that scattered Israel, parted his land and sold his people will be judged: “swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head.”

precepts.text: Tyre and Zidon and the coasts of Palestine took the Most High's silver and gold and carried His goodly pleasant things into their temples.
precepts.point: We are living this now. Every time a foreign king came up to invade Israel he stripped the silver and gold and pleasant things out of the temple and exacted tribute. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours be in the house of a stranger”. Your labours are the riches that come from your work ending up in the house of strangers.

Joel shows it happening: “Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head; Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things”. Tyre and Zidon and the coasts of Palestine took the Most High's silver and gold and carried his goodly pleasant things into their temples. Every time a foreign king came up to invade Israel he stripped the silver and gold and pleasant things out of the temple and exacted tribute.

We are living this now. In this captivity Esau still profits off our labour and our inventions, the light filament, the plasma and open heart surgery, the cotton gin, computers and cell phones, yet makes no account of who produced them. Strangers are filled with our wealth, and the Most High promises to return their recompence on their own head.

precepts.text: Tyre, Zidon, and the coasts of Palestine, the modern-day Arabs of Ishmael, sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem to the Grecians, the white people united under Alexander; God returns their recompense on their own head.
precepts.point: The word "world" means a group of people with common goals or interests, like the sports world or basketball world, so "world without end" and God so loved the world are not speaking of everybody but of Israel.

note.label: Isaiah 45: I Form the Light and Create Darkness

precepts.why:
“The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall come after thee; in chains they shall come over”. This is prophecy that the Africans, the men of stature, come over in chains, because they sold us into slavery to the so-called white man, the Grecians. Joel names the sellers: “Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head”.

Tyre, Zidon and the coasts of Palestine are the modern-day Arabs of Ishmael. “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” They sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem to the Grecians, the white people united under Alexander, and took “my silver and my gold” into their temples. God returns their recompense on their own head, and so they come over in chains, fall down and make supplication, “saying, Surely God is in thee; and there is none else, there is no God.”

The makers of idols “shall be ashamed, and also confounded”, but “Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation”, world without end. The word “world” means a group of people with common goals or interests, like the sports world or basketball world, so “world without end” and God so loved the world are not speaking of everybody but of Israel.

precepts.text: The heathen are gathered to the valley of Jehoshaphat where the Most High sits to judge, the reverse of beating weapons into farm tools.
precepts.point: Israel takes no wood out of the field because they burn the weapons for fuel, and they spoil those that spoiled them and rob those that robbed them. It is a turning: those who took from us, we take from them.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
Joel gives the gathering that ends this way: “Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up”. The heathen are gathered to the valley of Jehoshaphat where the Most High sits to judge. It is the reverse of beating weapons into farm tools; the Gentiles are told to prepare war.

And this is what becomes of their war. “Behold, it is come, and it is done”; those that dwell in the cities of Israel go forth and burn the weapons, “the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears”, with fire seven years. Their weapons are taken from them. They will be beaten into submission and forced to work the land instead of making war.

Israel takes no wood out of the field because they burn the weapons for fuel, and “they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them”. It is a turning: those who took from us, we take from them.

precepts.text: The Most High gathers all nations to the valley of Jehoshaphat and pleads with them there, because they scattered his people and parted his land, so the nations are brought down for judgment.
precepts.point: The times of the gentiles being fulfilled is not their salvation but their judgment: the Most High breaks the nations in his land. If salvation only means being saved to enslave us, that is not salvation, and it makes no sense that Christ would save the same gentile nations he prophesied would enslave Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.”

The nations are brought down for judgment, because they scattered his people and parted his land. Israel is his heritage; the nations are the ones who scattered them. So the fulfilling of the times of the gentiles is their judgment, and the restitution of all things is Israel's heritage and land given back.

precepts.text: The children of Judah were sold unto the Grecians, marking a distinction between literal Greeks of Edom and the Grecians of Acts 6.
precepts.point: Those who argue the Most High deals with the Greeks too are themselves so-called African American, West Indian, Haitian, and Jamaican, and they do not fit the title. To claim the grafting you must prove by your records which Gentile nation you are, and each Gentile nation had judgments that are not yet fulfilled.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
How Israelites came to be in Greece: “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.”

Judah was sold unto the Grecians, the literal Greeks of Edom, and removed far from their border. That marks the distinction: the Grecians Judah was sold to are the Greeks, and the Grecians of Acts 6 are the children of Judah who were sold there and took the name of the land, murmuring against the Hebrews over their widows.
